cohort: The study included 2198 low-risk pregnant women, distinguishing between primiparous and multiparous women.
finding: Flexible sacrum positions at birth increase maternal well-being by reducing perineal tearing and shortening the second stage of labor, without affecting neonatal health.
mod_finding: In primiparous women, the all-fours position was associated with an intact perineum and a shorter second stage of labor, while in multiparous women, the side-lying position was correlated with an intact perineum.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was considered as a variable and adjusted for in the analysis, but no specific weight range for inclusion was mentioned.
